result:
A live broadcast can now go back to draft, and launching replaces any earlier schedule. I haven't run the type check, lint or tests, and I didn't add a test.

**Back to draft.** The read-only summary page has a "Stop and edit" button while the broadcast is active. It sets the broadcast to `draft`, so the scene swaps back to the wizard on the review step, or on the first step with an error. The button is disabled while runs are loading or a send is in flight. Changes are in `BroadcastSummary.tsx` and `broadcastWizardLogic.ts` (new `returnToDraft` action and `returningToDraft` state).

**Schedule replaced on launch.** `launchBroadcast` now deletes the broadcast's existing schedules before setting it to `active`. It then creates the new schedule, or dispatches the batch job for "send now". This fixes the silent no-op: a schedule paused by an audience edit is deleted rather than left paused, and an old schedule can't fire alongside the new one. The schedule ids come from the response of the save that runs at the start of launch. If a delete fails, the broadcast is still a draft and the existing error toast appears.

I edited the hand-maintained kea typegen interfaces in the logic file to include the new action and value. A typegen run may reformat them.

I chose the "Stop and edit" label and the toast wording myself, and I did not run the `/writing-user-facing-copy` skill, so please review both.
